newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, taxes revised.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, taxes revised.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were stable in late trading on Monday, with the industry welcoming a reduction in the export tax on crude palm oil and products.
They said palm olein was quoted at 1,360-70 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening but higher than last Friday's closing level of 1,350 rupiah.
The government announced that it was restructing the export tax on crude palm oil and its products, lowering them from the average 10-12 percent range recorded between 1994 and 1996.
Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said crude palm oil would be subject to an export tax of five percent, palm olein two percent, palm oil and crude olein four percent each.
The changes were part of the government's latest package of economic deregulation measures unveiled on Monday.
Traders said the new tax structure would raise Indonesia's export competitiveness for palm products, especially olein.

"I think we will see a slight decline in overseas' palm olein prices because of the new tax structure," one trader said. "But local olein prices could increase because the expected rise in exports could result in a shortage domestically."

The traders said they were waiting for the July export taxes, adding that the new tax formula was likely to be used in calculating the rates. The finance ministry usually releases the rates in the first week of each month.
